newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid bourse strides up in optimistic mood.
newsitem.headline: Madrid bourse strides up in optimistic mood.

text.p: The Madrid bourse closed higher on Tuesday with clear advances in most sectors amid a prevailing optimistic mood.
The market expected the Bank of Spain to cut rates after the budget was presented on Friday, and did not flinch when the central bank left them alone earlier on Tuesday.

Dealers said there were signs the market could near year highs in the short term, as long as there were no surprises from a Federal Open Market Committee on U.S. rates, at which a small hike was expected.
The general index gained 2.89 points, 0.81 percent, to 361.78 and the Ibex-35 rose 37.74 points, 0.92 percent, to 4,135.72.
"There's been a lot of animation in the bourse today. No one wants to sell and, except for surprises from the Fed, we can continue this tendency for the short term," one dealer said.
The market slipped a bit on the U.S. consumer confidence data, but then bounced back to close near highs.
Trading volume reached more than 31.3 billion pesetas, most of it in Telefonica, Iberdrola and Endesa shares.
Electricity shares Iberdrola and Sevillana rose more than 2.0 percent.
